_comment: Declared invariants that currently have NO code reader. An entry here means READ AND CLASSIFIED,
never EXEMPT — each names the M-register entry holding the open decision, and each is a live
finding that has simply been made visible instead of left silent. This list only shrinks.
WHY THESE ARE BASELINED RATHER THAN FIXED. Each needs a decision that was not the check
author's to take. Shipping the check red would have forced rushed answers; shipping it with
this file forces none, and makes the NEXT instance fail on arrival — which is the whole value,
since every one of these went unnoticed for months precisely because nothing ever asked the
question out loud. (This paragraph said 'THESE THREE' until 2026-08-23; HELP_CONTENT_DRAFT
gained a real reader and left, and the count in the prose did not follow it out. A hardcoded
number describing the contents of the file it sits in is the same defect class as M-082.)
⚠ A CHECK IS NOT A CALLER. Both remaining entries have since acquired a MECHANISM that reads
them (see each reason), and neither is thereby healed: the ratchet asks whether the declared
invariant governs the system's BEHAVIOUR, and a gate asserting two artefacts agree does not
make either one load-bearing at runtime. Do not close an entry by widening 'read' to include
the checks — that weakens the ratchet to retire the findings that motivated it.
TO REMOVE AN ENTRY: wire a real reader. The check then FAILS until the line is deleted from here,
which is the ratchet — a baseline that silently tolerated a healed entry would drift back to
meaning nothing. Do NOT remove an entry by deleting the export: that removes the record of the
rule and leaves the obligation, which is strictly worse than the gap it closes.

excludePlatformOrg.reason: A stated MUST ('every for-each-org query MUST exclude the platform org') with zero call sites. The census ran 2026-08-23 and the answer was NOT 'already safe': the platform org (0 members, 44 days old against a 60-day threshold) was returned live by find_dormant_org_candidates(now()) and was on a scheduled path to being purged. Fixed — but in SQL (is_platform = false in both dormancy RPCs, a RAISE in purge_org_cascade) plus a TS guard in purgeOrg, because the defect was in a SECURITY DEFINER function that this TypeScript helper cannot reach. So the hole is closed and THIS EXPORT IS STILL UNREAD, which makes it more misleading than before, not less: a reader now finds a stated MUST, no callers, and a protected system, and would reasonably conclude the helper is what protects it. M-067 stays open for the general rule and for that.

RETENTION_PROTECTED_TABLES.reason: A PPRA/POPIA statutory retention list with no importer, which THREE artefacts asserted was live in the present tense — the array's own comment, the module's file header, and 010_platform_features.sql — all three now corrected. M-082's stated fix ('purge sites derive the skip-list from this array by import') is NOT BUILDABLE: purge_org_cascade is a SQL SECURITY DEFINER function and cannot import a TypeScript array. What shipped 2026-08-23 instead is scripts/check-retention-skiplist.mts, which asserts this array equals BOTH copies of the same list inside that function. The entry stays because a check is not a caller — the purge does not derive its behaviour from these six strings, it is merely forbidden to disagree with them.
